item.text: I’m checking 2024 Egypt sources directly for whether Sisi’s policy mix points to broad-based, durable prosperity or to short-term stabilization, patronage, and coercive regime maintenance. I’ll keep this bounded to a few targeted searches and then synthesize only the strongest claim-level items.

item.text:
**5B.1 — Mixed, but leaning no**
2024 contains real evidence of a technocratic, reform-oriented macro package: private-sector growth, social protection, SOE reform, and a better business environment. But the same record shows heavy reliance on external financing, continued state-footprint concerns, high inflation/debt pressure, and crackdowns when economic discontent surfaced. That looks more like stabilization and regime maintenance than a clean shift toward broad-based, sustainable prosperity.

**Supports 5B.1**
- **World Bank Group Statement of Support to Egypt’s Development and Reform Efforts** | World Bank Group | 2024-03-18 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2024/03/18/world-bank-group-statement-of-support-to-egypt-s-development-and-reform-efforts | The Bank says Egypt’s partnership is aimed at inclusive growth, private-sector job creation, human capital, resilience, and protection of the poorest and most vulnerable. That is strong public evidence that the 2024 policy frame was not just rent extraction. | `5B.1`
- **Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt through Cash Transfer Programs** | World Bank Group | 2024-05-28 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs | The Takaful and Karama program is described as institutionalized, well-targeted, and linked to health, education, and women’s empowerment. This is one of the clearest pro-broad-based-prosperity signals, though it is social protection rather than structural transformation. | `5B.1`
- **IMF Staff and the Egyptian Authorities Reach Staff Level Agreement on the First and Second Reviews under the EFF Arrangement** | IMF | 2024-03-06 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/06/pr-2459-egypt-staff-and-authorities-reach-agreement-on-reviews-under-the-eff-arrangement | The IMF says the authorities agreed to more social spending for vulnerable groups, a larger cash-transfer package, and reforms to level the playing field and remove preferential treatment for state-owned enterprises. That supports an intent to build broader prosperity rather than simply buy loyalty. | `5B.1`
- **IMF Reaches Staff Level Agreement on the Third Review of the Extended Fund Facility with Egypt** | IMF | 2024-06-06 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/06/pr-24208-egypt-imf-reaches-agreement-on-the-3rd-review-of-the-eff | The IMF says the reform agenda was to raise private-sector-led growth, generate fiscal space for health, education, and targeted social spending, and improve the business environment by reducing the state’s role. This is the strongest direct pro-reform evidence in the 2024 record. | `5B.1`
- **IMF Executive Board Completes the Third Review of the Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility for Egypt** | IMF | 2024-07-29 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24293-egypt-imf-exec-board-completes-3rd-rev-extended-arr-eff | The IMF says stabilization was starting to help, inflation was easing, foreign-exchange shortages had been eliminated, and investor confidence was improving. This is real progress, but it is still stabilization, not proof of durable broad-based prosperity. | `5B.1`

**Cuts against 5B.1**
- **Arab Republic of Egypt: First and Second Reviews Under the Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-03-29 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/29/pr24101-egypt-imf-executive-board-completes-first-second-reviews-eff-approves-augmentation | The IMF says Egypt’s plan required reducing public investment, and specifically says withdrawing the state and military from economic activity is key. That is strong evidence that the inherited economy still relied on state/military dominance and that sustainable private-led prosperity was not yet secured. | `5B.1`
- **Macro Poverty Outlook for Arab Republic of Egypt : April 2024** | World Bank | 2024-04-03 | https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099759004052420744 | The World Bank describes growth as falling to 2.8 percent in FY24 because of eroded real incomes. That undercuts any claim that 2024 delivered broad-based prosperity in practice. | `5B.1`
- **IMF Executive Board Completes the Third Review of the Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility for Egypt** | IMF | 2024-07-29 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24293-egypt-imf-exec-board-completes-3rd-rev-extended-arr-eff | The IMF says inflation was still elevated and that continued fiscal consolidation was needed to create room for social programs. That means the 2024 gains were fragile and not yet transformed into broad prosperity. | `5B.1`
- **IMF Reaches Staff Level Agreement on the Fourth Review of the Extended Fund Facility with Egypt** | IMF | 2024-12-24 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/12/24/pr24500-egypt-imf-reaches-sla-on-the-fourth-review-on-the-eff | The IMF says Egypt still needed to accelerate divestment, reduce the state footprint, and improve the business environment, while creating fiscal space for social programs. This reads as unfinished structural adjustment rather than a settled prosperity model. | `5B.1`
- **Egypt halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis** | Amnesty International | 2024-05-13 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/ | Amnesty says authorities arrested protesters, striking workers, and online critics over economic discontent. That suggests the regime responded to economic pain with coercion, which fits short-term control more than broad-based prosperity-building. | `5B.1`
- **Egypt: More than 100 arbitrarily detained over calls for anti-government protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-07-18 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/ | Amnesty says security forces detained 119 people after online protest calls and used incommunicado detention and broad security charges. That is evidence of regime-maintenance behavior when living standards worsened, not a prosperity-first political strategy. | `5B.1`
- **Egypt’s 2024 reforms were partly funded by a large external rescue package** | IMF / World Bank context | 2024-03 to 2024-07 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/29/pr24101-egypt-imf-executive-board-completes-first-second-reviews-eff-approves-augmentation | The repeated mention of the Ras El-Hekma deal and external financing shows the year’s economic stability depended heavily on outside capital and near-term balance-of-payments relief. That weakens any claim of self-sustaining prosperity creation. | `5B.1`

**Search gap**
- I did not find a clean 2024 primary source showing Sisi himself articulated a fully coherent long-horizon industrial strategy with measurable distributional gains already visible in-year.
- I also did not find strong direct evidence that 2024 was mainly classic patronage spending; the clearer pattern is a mix of IMF/WB-backed adjustment, targeted social transfers, and coercive containment of economic dissent.

**Bottom line**
- The best reading is: Sisi’s 2024 program did include some genuine prosperity-building intent, especially on private-sector growth and targeted social protection, but the year’s actual pattern was still dominated by stabilization, external financing, and state-preservation. On balance, that is weaker evidence for “broad-based, sustainable prosperity” than for a short-term stabilization and control strategy.
